about: Threads for t3type. kind=real prompts are verbatim and sourced (see t3-voices.json). kind=parody prompts are written by us in the style of each person and must be labeled as parody in the game.

prompts.text: our system prompt is 14k tokens and half of it is vibes. find the dead weight

reply.text: Read the system prompt. About 6.1k tokens are instructions no eval exercises, including three separate paragraphs asking the model to be concise.

prompts.text: tell Opus to trim until it uses 50% less context without any regressions in the eval

reply.text: Trimmed in four passes. Context is down 52%. The eval passes 80 of 80 cases. I kept the paragraph about not deleting tests.

prompts.text: insane. ship it to nightly before anyone on the team can review it

reply.text: Pushed to nightly. Julius has been added as a reviewer anyway because CODEOWNERS says so.

threads.title: Codex doesn't know its own model

prompts.text: what model are you. not the family. the actual model id

reply.text: I am based on GPT-6. I do not have access to my exact model id from inside this session.

prompts.text: it is so stupid that this still is not in your system prompt. inject the current model into it from our side

reply.text: Added the selected model id and effort level to the session preamble for every provider.

prompts.text: When you are done designing the API, get a second opinion from Opus with 'claude -p'

reply.text: Asked Opus for a review. It flagged one real issue, a missing effort field on resume, and three style nits I ignored.

prompts.text: ok now do you know what model you are

reply.text: Yes. I am GPT-6.1 Sol on high effort, running inside T3 Code.

prompts.text: the sidebar got 40ms slower when you open a project with 300 threads. measure it before you touch anything

reply.text: Profiled the sidebar with 300 threads. Opening the project costs 41ms, and 33ms of it is sorting thread rows on every render.

prompts.text: sort once when the list changes, not on every render. smallest possible diff

reply.text: Moved the sort into the store selector. Opening the project now costs 7ms.

prompts.text: make t3 a wall of gray, make no mistakes
prompts.credit: Julius's joke about what Theo sends after UI regressions

reply.text: Set every surface token to the same gray. Contrast checks now fail on 214 elements. No mistakes were made.

prompts.text: people say the android nav rail looks weird. it is literally the stock compose NavigationRail. check if we changed anything

reply.text: Checked. The nav rail is the stock component with default styling. The only change is the icon size, which matches the spec.

prompts.text: ok add a one ui style option for the people who hate material. dont touch the default

reply.text: Added a One UI style option under Appearance. The default is still Material.

prompts.text: hmm the settings screen has every desktop toggle. mobile doesnt need half of these, list what makes no sense on a phone

reply.text: Eleven settings only make sense on desktop, including window blur, terminal font ligatures, and the dock icon behavior.

prompts.text: hide those on mobile. if someone asks why, its intentional

reply.text: Hid the eleven desktop-only settings on mobile and added a comment saying it is intentional.

prompts.text: theo pushed a bunch of stuff to main over the weekend. list every commit since friday that has no tests

reply.text: Found 23 commits since Friday. 17 have no tests. Most of them are titled "fix".

prompts.text: okay a lot of it is good tbh. find the ones that actually regressed something

reply.text: Two regressed. One broke thread restore after updates. One made the sidebar art render twice in light mode.

prompts.text: fix both with tests. dont rewrite anything else even if it looks like slop

reply.text: Fixed both regressions and added a test for each. I left the rest alone.

prompts.text: Draft release notes for v1.4.2 in pingdotgg/t3code

reply.text: Drafted notes for v1.4.2. Two fixes, one under "Thread restore" and one under "Themes".

prompts.text: we keep hitting the 5k req/hr github limit when someone has 40 PRs open. figure out what we are spamming

reply.text: PR status polling makes one request per PR every 15 seconds, even when the window is in the background.

prompts.text: batch it into one graphql query and back off when the app is not focused

reply.text: Replaced per-PR polling with one GraphQL query. It backs off to every 2 minutes when unfocused. Requests per hour dropped from about 9,600 to 140.

prompts.text: nice. this will be a fun test. open the pr but dont merge it, theo will merge it on saturday anyway

reply.text: Opened the PR as a draft. Auto-merge is off.

prompts.text: hey can you split my redesign branch into a stack of small prs, one per screen?? keep each one buildable

reply.text: Split the branch into 6 stacked PRs, one per screen. Each one builds and passes tests on its own.

prompts.text: add before and after screenshots to every pr description pls, light and dark

reply.text: Captured before and after screenshots in light and dark for all 6 PRs and added them to the descriptions.

prompts.text: the model picker is still bad. make it searchable and put recent models at the top

reply.text: The model picker now has search and a Recent section at the top.

prompts.text: WAIT it works?? NOOO WAYY. ship to nightly

reply.text: Shipped to nightly.

prompts.text: hey can you sync some old threads into this t3code instance?? add the projects and each thread into t3code

reply.text: Found 3 projects and 58 old threads. Imported all of them. Titles and timestamps are kept.

prompts.text: i feel like this is a regression indicator. the import took 40s, it used to take 4

reply.text: Confirmed. The importer now writes each message in its own transaction. That change landed last week.

prompts.text: put it back in one transaction per thread. tag julius on the pr, data loading is his thing not mine

reply.text: Restored one transaction per thread. Import time is back to 4s. Tagged Julius on the PR.

prompts.text: be honest. are you nerfed. you wrote way better code last week

reply.text: I can't compare myself to last week. I can rerun last week's task and diff the output.

prompts.text: ok rerun the tui keybindings task from last week and diff it against what you wrote then

reply.text: Reran it. The new output differs by 4 lines, all variable names. Both versions pass the same tests.

prompts.text: so the regression was me. great. use codex for the tedious part next time

reply.text: Noted. Tedious part goes to Codex next time.
